extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and administrators (postdocs, early-career investigators, PIs, grants officers)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical advice and procedural standards for submitting, interpreting reviews, and managing NIH grant awards (K- and R-series, SBIR/STTR, fellowships) including interactions with Program Officials, Grants Management, and institutional administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss score and next steps with Program Official (PO)
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving your summary statement, ask your PO about next steps and whether your score is competitive or if you should pursue other options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POs may not know final funding likelihood until IC budgets are finalized, but they can advise whether the score is 'worth waiting' or whether you should prepare a resubmission or pursue jobs. Use the summary statement to frame the conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Job search while K99 pending signals reduced training need
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting a job search while your K99 is pending signals you don't need additional training and will likely remove you from consideration for the K99 portion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your PO tells you it’s OK to search after funding, proceed; otherwise, recognize that actively job-hunting will 'almost certainly' get you dropped from award consideration. If PO suggests pursuing jobs, apply and cite the K99 score on job materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing an unfunded K99 on job applications
rubrics_metrics.description: You may list a scored but unfunded K99 application on faculty job applications, including application number, title, and score in the research funding section of your CV and possibly in letters or research statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not refer to a K99 score within other NIH grant applications (to avoid confusing reviewers about prior/submitted work). Use it strategically in job contexts to show competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret Summary of Discussion as panel consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: If a misconception appears in the Summary of Discussion, it generally means the entire panel agreed with that weakness; if a weakness appears only in an individual critique it was not score-driving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot usually ‘appeal’ such panel-agreed points; instead, address these issues in a future resubmission and get fresh eyes to ensure clarity. Ignore individual criterion scores for score-driving interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid formal appeals to review outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals are generally not effective and are 'never a good idea' as a response to reviewer misunderstanding or unfavorable scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If warranted, discuss with your PO only in the context of whether a short rebuttal to the review would help for possible select pay consideration; otherwise focus on revising and resubmitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PO-advised rebuttals selectively (for select pay or clarification)
rubrics_metrics.description: A short rebuttal to clarify reviewer misconceptions may be appropriate only if the PO recommends it (e.g., for select pay consideration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send unsolicited appeals. If the PO suggests a rebuttal, keep it brief and focused on clarifying key factual errors that could influence funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paylines depend on IC budget and are provisional
rubrics_metrics.description: Paylines are conservative at the outset of the fiscal year until the federal budget is signed into law and IC appropriations are finalized; when paylines are raised later they are usually applied retroactively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume early-year paylines are final; consult your PO after summary statements for guidance and plan resubmissions rather than waiting on uncertain paylines.

rubrics_metrics.name: K99/K22/K-award paylines and slot-based funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition awards like K22 and K99 may be handled differently (ICs often have a set number of slots) so payline statements like 'K except K22 and K99' reflect slot management and differing considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because these awards are for postdocs transitioning to faculty, ICs may exercise more flexibility. Ask your PO about how their IC manages K99 slots and competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons status (Council review completed/pending) is ambiguous
rubrics_metrics.description: Statuses such as 'Council review completed' or 'Pending' do not guarantee funding: 'Council review completed' can mean electronic en-bloc approval but does not ensure an award will be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICs send larger lists to Council than they can fund; 'not considered' cannot be issued until the fiscal year completes, so early status changes are not definitive. Look for JIT requests or status changes to 'Pending'/'Award prepared' for clearer signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of awards depends on fiscal year and appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if reviewed and approved, awards are often delayed until after the federal budget is passed; Cycle 1 applications may sometimes be awarded in September but frequently awards occur in December or early next year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for delays tied to budget timing; add ~2 months after presidential signing for ICs to receive final appropriation and process awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: GMS and Grants Management Specialist roles and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A GMS (Grants Management Specialist) is assigned to scored applications; they handle administrative review and award preparation but typically cannot provide funding timing details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GMS will contact you if they need additional information (JIT requests, human/animal approvals). For funding likelihood questions, speak to your PO rather than GMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: When status is 'pending administrative review', 'sit tight' unless asked
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is 'pending administrative review', usually no action is required from the PI until GMS/PO asks for additional information; ICs process many awards and timing can be lengthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can check with your grants office or PO if you suspect issues (e.g., animal/human subject compliance) but expect processing to continue up to Sept 30 for FY decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT and 'Award prepared' timelines can take weeks
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission of JIT materials, the Commons status may not change immediately; the 'Award prepared' stage can last up to a week or more while IC Director's office completes final approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a couple of weeks or into September; the GMO's actions may not change Commons status each time they access the system. If the GMO requests nothing more, the remaining delay is IC administrative processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC-specific variability: some ICs don't publish paylines
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all ICs publish paylines for every mechanism; some ICs explicitly say 'no fixed payline' and consider scientific merit, program priorities, portfolio balance, and funds availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your IC does not publish a payline, talk to your PO about program priorities and how funding decisions are made beyond impact score alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR funding decisions use broader criteria beyond score
rubrics_metrics.description: For SBIR/STTR (R41/R42/R43/R44) NICHD (example) states there is no fixed payline; funding decisions consider scientific merit, program priorities, strategic plan, portfolio balance, and availability of funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even a good score may not guarantee funding if programmatic concerns (e.g., multiple overlapping SBIRs, 'SBIR mill' history, portfolio balance) weigh against an applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission planning after summary statement
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving the summary statement you should plan resubmission strategies and discuss them with your PO, rather than waiting months for payline changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POs often recommend resubmission for 'insurance' given uncertainty in paylines; use reviewer comments to guide revisions and consider alternative FOAs if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective pay decisions are unpredictable and typically end-of-year
rubrics_metrics.description: Select pay (special funding of an application outside the normal payline) decisions are typically considered late in the fiscal year and are often made by IC leadership rather than the PO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A PO might raise select pay for a high-interest application, but you should not rely on select pay; have a resubmission plan in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage overlapping awards and PI effort proactively
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are PI on multiple awards and a new award is pending, you must reallocate effort (or terminate/modify existing awards) so you are not overcommitted when new funding arrives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with your institutional fiscal/grant administrator to reassign effort, consider terminating NCE awards early if necessary, and prepare for possible JIT requests that will require accurate effort allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: T32 and fellowship (F32) activation timing considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: T32 programs should not knowingly appoint someone for less than 9 months; leaving a T32 quickly after starting may be administratively sensitive but is often acceptable if a trainee secures individual fellowship funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask the T32 director whether early termination (activating an F32 sooner) would cause problems for reporting/budgeting, and consider whether you truly need the extra months of training/data before activating the fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRG (study section) assignment can be contested with evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is assigned to an SRG you believe lacks appropriate expertise, you can request CSR to move it — but you must demonstrate how the current panel lacks the needed expertise and that the preferred panel has it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue with specific, evidence-based reasons (not just 'my work won't be appreciated'). Consult your PO about whether the reassignment is appropriate before requesting CSR intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of individual criterion scores vs. overall impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual reviewer criterion scores are not necessarily score-driving; the Summary of Discussion and overall impact determine panel consensus and the final score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a weakness appears only in one critique, it likely didn't drive the score; focus on the Summary of Discussion when deciding how to revise the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visa and eligibility issues handled during R00/award phase
rubrics_metrics.description: For K99 applicants on visas (e.g., J-1 with 2-year home residency), visa/work-authorization issues are typically resolved by the institution during the R00/award acceptance and hiring phase; POs generally focus on funding first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions will often assist with waivers/H1B processing after funding. Provide required documentation when requested; earlier proof (no-objection letters) can be helpful but is usually not required during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council sends large candidate lists; being sent does not equal selection
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs send Council lists much longer than the number they will fund; being on the Council list means you cleared initial hurdles but is not a guarantee of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that Council approval is a necessary but not sufficient step; continued IC review, programmatic balancing, and final appropriations determine award decisions.
